issue.title: Update: XML_Security_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The XML Security Cheat Sheet is about 5,600 words with 408 lines of code.

- "Dealing with invalid XML documents" is about 3,800 words in one section, much of it schema data-type detail (NaN, divide by zero, prefixed values, ranges).
- The XXE and entity expansion part is about 1,600 words, including four full vulnerable Java parser samples (DOM, DOM4J, SAX, StAX). The [XML External Entity Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/XML_External_Entity_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) cheat sheet already covers safe parser setup per language, and this sheet never links it.

## How should this be resolved?

- Replace the XXE and entity expansion samples with a short summary of the attacks and a link to the XXE Prevention cheat sheet.
- Condense schema validation to the principles: use a strict local schema, restrict types and lengths, and limit sizes and nesting. Keep one short example at most.
- Keep the malformed document and jumbo payload guidance, but shorter.

Small PRs, one section at a time, please. They are much easier to review than one big rewrite :)

2904.title: XML Security: condense XXE/entity-expansion section, link the XXE Prevention cheat sheet
2904.body:
# You're A Rockstar

Thank you for submitting a Pull Request (PR) to the Cheat Sheet Series.

> :triangular_flag_on_post: If your PR is related to grammar/typo mistakes, please double-check the file for other mistakes in order to fix all the issues in the current cheat sheet.

Please make sure that for your contribution:

- [x] In case of a new Cheat Sheet, you have used the [Cheat Sheet template](../templates/New_CheatSheet.md). — N/A, no new sheet.
- [x] All the markdown files do not raise any validation policy violation, see the [policy](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/actions?query=workflow%3A%22Markdown+Link+Check%22).
- [x] All the markdown files follow these [format rules](../CONTRIBUTING.md#markdown).
- [x] All your assets are stored in the **assets** folder. — N/A, no assets in this PR.
- [x] All the images used are in the **PNG** format. — N/A, no images in this PR.
- [x] Any references to websites have been formatted as `[TEXT](URL)`
- [x] You verified/tested the effectiveness of your contribution (e.g., the defensive code proposed is really an effective remediation? Please verify it works!). — N/A in the narrow sense: this PR proposes no new remediation code. The four vulnerable Java samples and the attack walkthroughs are replaced by a summary that points to the [XML External Entity Prevention cheat sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/XML_External_Entity_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html), whose per-parser configurations are already the validated remediation for this sheet's audience.
- [x] The CI build of your PR pass, see the build status [here](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/actions). — will confirm once CI runs on this PR.

## Scope and sourcing (required)

- [x] This PR is focused: it modifies a single cheat sheet, or a small coordinated set, and the scope is described in the PR body.
- [x] Every technical claim, recommendation, or threat assertion added in this PR is supported by a primary source (RFC, NIST, OWASP standard, vendor documentation, peer-reviewed research) linked inline as `[text](URL)`.
- [x] I have read each source I cite and confirm it actually supports the claim. I have not relied on summaries, hearsay, or model-generated citations.

## What this PR does

Implements the **entity-expansion half** of #2796 (the schema-validation half is separately assigned and intentionally untouched):

- Replaces the four vulnerable Java parser samples (DOM, DOM4J, SAX, StAX), the Billion laughs / quadratic blowup payloads, and the SSRF/port-scanning walkthroughs (~370 lines) with a short conceptual section: one minimal illustrative document, the three consequence classes with CWE links, and the out-of-band/parameter-entity variant with a source.
- States the single countermeasure that all these attacks share (do not process DTDs or resolve external entities in application-facing parsers) and cross-links the [XML External Entity Prevention cheat sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/XML_External_Entity_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) for per-language configuration, per the "don't duplicate — link instead" rule.
- Every removed w3schools DTD link was inside the deleted content; no other files touched.

## Local checks

- `npm run lint-markdown`: passes.
- `npm run lint-terminology`: passes.
- `npm run link-check`: the checker's built-in Python extractor cannot spawn in this container-less environment (EPIPE), so each link I added was verified manually with HTTP GET and read: CWE-611 ("Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference"), CWE-776 ("Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs"), CWE-918 ("Server-Side Request Forgery"), the W3C XML 1.0 `#dt-entdecl` anchor (the entity-declaration definition in the spec body), the OWASP XXE Prevention sheet (its introduction names exactly these consequences), and the PortSwigger blind-XXE page (its "Exploiting blind XXE to exfiltrate data out-of-band" section covers the parameter-entity variant). Note: CWE-40 was deliberately not cited — verification showed it is a Windows UNC path-traversal weakness, not XXE.

## AI Tool Usage Disclosure (required for all PRs)

- [ ] I have NOT used any AI tool to generate the contents of this PR.
- [x] I have used AI tools to generate the contents of this PR. I have verified
    the contents and I affirm the results. The LLM used is `GLM (glm-5.3-flash-free), driving an OpenCode agent session on the contributor's device, 2026-11-06`
    and the prompt used is `the resolution plan in #2796 ("Replace the XXE and entity expansion samples with a short summary of the attacks and a link to the XXE Prevention cheat sheet"), applied under this repo's AGENTS.md rules (sources must be fetched and read, no fabricated URLs, keep it conceptual, disclose AI usage)`. I have independently verified every citation and technical claim against the cited source.

This PR fixes issue #2796 (entity-expansion part).

2907.title: docs: condense malformed XML document and jumbo payload guidance
2907.body:
Refs #2796

- condense guidance for handling malformed xml documents and fatal errors
- clarify that parsers must not continue normal processing after a fatal error, consistent with the [[w3c xml specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-terminology)](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-terminology)
- recommend disabling recovery or lenient parsing modes for untrusted input
- streamline coercive parsing guidance and add nesting depth and request size mitigations
- clarify jumbo payload threats as resource exhaustion through memory, cpu, and network bandwidth
- add mitigations for jumbo payloads, including request body limits, parser resource constraints, and streaming parsers
- reference [[oracle jaxp security guide](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-api-xml-processing-jaxp-security-guide.html)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-api-xml-processing-jaxp-security-guide.html) for parser limits such as `maxelementdepth` and `entityexpansionlimit`
- remove redundant examples, truncated snippets, and excessive formatting

## What this PR does

- Replaces the `Document without Schema` / `Unrestrictive Schema` / `Improper Data Validation` region (String and Numeric Data Types, Negative and Positive Restrictions, Prefixed Values, and the rest of the data-type walkthrough — ~270 lines) with the principles the issue asks for: **strict versioned local schema**, **reject rather than repair**, **facet-level value restrictions**, **type by meaning**, and **size/nesting limits delegated to parser configuration** with a cross-link to the [XXE Prevention cheat sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/XML_External_Entity_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).
